title: Compass and Monsoon
premise: Gideon Zhou, a bush pilot who delivers medicine and mail across a rainforest frontier, is hired to search for a vanished government survey team and finds only their gear arranged in a deliberate pattern — a message, not an accident. Grounded by the early monsoon, she teams up with Tomas Reyes, a river trader with his own reasons for distrusting the government, and follows the trail by boat into territory the maps refuse to name. They discover the survey team found something the state wants buried: evidence that a sanctioned mining operation poisoned the river villages Gideon has been supplying, and one survivor hiding with proof. Hunted by the official who ordered the disappearance, Gideon must choose between flying home to safety and carrying the evidence out through the storm; in the end she trades her plane for the truth, exposing the operation at the cost of the life she built, and finds that identity was never the miles but the choices.
about_author: Wren Sterling is the pen name of a former aid-logistics coordinator who spent six years ferrying supplies to river communities before turning to fiction. Their novels blend aviation detail, moral ambiguity, and landscapes that behave like characters.

chapters.title: Fuel, Rain, Rumors
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A routine medicine run into the interior establishes her world: the airstrip, the gossip economy of small planes, three years of measured distance since whatever she fled. She hears the first rumor of a missing survey team and dismisses it. Beat: restless competence masking avoidance.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A government liaison, Director Hale, offers her a lucrative search contract — too lucrative. She takes it despite instinct, needing the money to keep her plane airworthy. First glimpse of Hale's controlled menace. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Grid Search
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV over three days of flying. She finds the survey camp: tents intact, gear stacked neatly, no bodies, no tracks, a compass needle reversed on the map table like a signature. Radio log's last entry cut mid-word. Beat: dread crystallizing into obsession.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The monsoon arrives weeks early; the strip floods and her engine throws a rod on landing. Stranded at the river town of Puerto Lobo, she meets Tomas Reyes, whose trading boat is the only way forward. He refuses money but not, oddly, the story. Beat: pride bending to necessity.

chapters.title: The Stranger's Price
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He agrees to take her upstream because he recognized the reversed-compass detail — his brother was on a previous survey team that vanished the same way. He hides this from Gideon. Beat: guilt steering a man who claims to be free.

chapters.title: Leaking Hull
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The boat journey begins; the hull seeps, the river rises, and they learn each other's rhythms under strain. Gideon notices Tomas knows the river too well for a mere trader. Beat: wary partnership forming in shared labor.

chapters.title: Village of the Quiet
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They stop at a village where children show skin lesions she recognizes from the medicine crates — symptoms of heavy-metal poisoning from upstream. The villagers won't say the mine's name aloud. Beat: the mission stops being about the missing team.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Night conversation; he almost tells Gideon about his brother, instead tells her why he left government service. She admits, obliquely, that she once had a duty she abandoned. Two liars circling honesty. Beat: intimacy without confession.

chapters.title: The Second Camp
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They find a second abandoned site — older, overgrown, with the same reversed compass and a rusted tag bearing a name Tomas goes white at seeing. His brother's. The pattern spans years. Beat: personal stakes detonate.

chapters.title: Hale's Shadow
chapters.summary: Hale's POV (first antagonist chapter). In the capital, Hale learns Gideon went upstream instead of returning, burns the search file, and dispatches men to 'recover' the situation. We see the machinery of erasure working calmly. Beat: cold institutional menace.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In a cave behind a waterfall, they find Dr. Amara Osei, the survey team's geologist, half-starved, guarding water samples and a ledger proving the mine — state-sanctioned — poisoned the watershed and that prior survey teams were disappeared to bury it. Beat: revelation as burden.

chapters.title: Duty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Amara's POV flashback woven into present. She explains why she ran rather than reported: every channel led back to Hale. She asks Gideon to fly the evidence out when the weather breaks. Gideon calculates what it will cost and says yes anyway. Beat: love of truth against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Pursuit on the Water
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Hale's men reach the river; a night chase through flooded channels, engine trouble, a near-drowning where Tomas saves Gideon and loses the spare fuel. They're committed now — no fuel to turn back. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sheltering from the worst squall, truths surface: Gideon's past as a government pilot who flew the orders that destroyed a village and fled; Tomas's brother, whom he reported for dissent and who then vanished. Forgiveness neither asks nor grants, but shares. Beat: identity stripped to its bones.

chapters.title: The Mine
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They pass the mining operation itself — fenced, floodlit, chemically dead water below it. Amara documents; Gideon photographs from the boat. A patrol spots them. Beat: horror made concrete, clock now audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Betrayal's Shape
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. One of Tomas's river contacts sells their position to Hale's men for medicine for his own sick child. The party scatters; Amara is captured with a decoy ledger while the real samples stay hidden. Beat: despair, and the question of what betrayal means under desperation.

chapters.title: The Long Portage
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Carrying the boat and evidence overland around rapids, pursued on foot, Gideon's piloting hands prove useless in jungle and Tomas's knowledge proves useless against exhaustion; they save each other alternately. Beat: love acknowledged wordlessly under load.

chapters.title: Radio Silence Broken
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At a derelict missionary station, Gideon repairs an ancient transmitter and reaches her old mentor, arranging a meeting at a coastal strip — but Hale intercepts the transmission and sets his trap there. She knows it might be a trap and plans anyway. Beat: gambit accepted.

chapters.title: The Strip at Storm's Edge
chapters.summary: Climax part one, Gideon's POV. The coastal rendezvous becomes a standoff: Hale offers Gideon her old life, her record expunged, in exchange for the samples. Tomas walks into the open as distraction; Amara, captive, signals the decoy ledger's location falsely. Beat: everything staked.

chapters.title: Compass True
chapters.summary: Climax part two, alternating POV. In the chaos of the storm's final violence, Gideon chooses the truth over the deal, broadcasting the ledger's contents on the open band before Hale can silence her; his men waver as the transmission lands on every radio in the region. Hale falls not to violence but to exposure. Beat: justice outside the law, paid for in blood and metal.

chapters.title: Wreckage and Witness
chapters.summary: Falling action, Tomas's POV. The inquiry begins; Amara testifies; the mine closes. Gideon's plane is confiscated as evidence and never returned. She and Tomas stand in the wreckage of her old life and find it lighter than expected. Beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: Miles, Then Years
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV coda. Months later, she co-runs a supply run by boat with Tomas, delivering medicine to the recovering villages, measuring life in seasons now instead of miles. A new pilot asks why she left flying; she answers honestly. Final image: the river ahead, the compass true. Beat: identity rebuilt on choice.
